run.question: What is the distribution of events by service in the 'app-183d-events' index? Give me the count of events for each service.

report.summary: In the Elasticsearch index 'app-183d-events' the documents group into three service values over the authorized window 2026-10-24T17:12:58Z to 2026-11-23T17:12:58Z: payment-api 5 events, order-service 3 events, inventory-api 2 events, out of 10 total matched documents. The index reports docs.count 10 and the aggregation total is also 10, so the counts appear to cover the whole index, though document counts are only current state. Fields available in the mapping are duration_ms (integer), event_type (keyword), service (keyword) and timestamp (date); every document returned carries event_type 'request'. Note the tool applies a mandatory time filter on the 'timestamp' date field: the default one-hour window (2026-11-23T16:12:58Z to 17:12:58Z) matched only 2 documents, both inventory-api, which is a narrower sample than the counts reported here. This is a distribution question, not a fault investigation; no root cause is asserted.

claims.text: The index 'app-183d-events' exists (health green, status open) with docs.count 10 and store.size 6.3kb at query time.

The mapping of 'app-183d-events' defines properties duration_ms (integer), event_type (keyword), service (keyword) and timestamp (date); 'service' is therefore a keyword field usable for exact terms aggregation.

Aggregating 'app-183d-events' by the 'service' field over the full authorized window (2026-10-24T17:12:58Z to 2026-11-23T17:12:58Z, time filter applied to 'timestamp') returned total 10 documents with buckets payment-api=5, order-service=3, inventory-api=2, and sum_other_doc_count 0 at aggregation size 50.

The 10 individual documents returned from 'app-183d-events' (sorted by timestamp ascending) are: payment-api at 2026-11-23T15:10, 15:11, 15:12, 15:13 and 15:14; order-service at 16:10, 16:11 and 16:12; inventory-api at 17:10 and 17:11; all have event_type 'request'.

With the default one-hour window (time filter on 'timestamp' from 2026-11-23T16:12:58Z to 2026-11-23T17:12:58Z) the same aggregation matched only 2 documents, both in the inventory-api bucket; those two are the 17:10 and 17:11 inventory-api documents.

gaps: All 10 of the index's 10 documents carry timestamps between 2026-11-23T15:10Z and 2026-11-23T17:11Z; whether the index ever contained events outside the authorized window (for example older events already rolled off, or future ones) cannot be determined from these queries.
Elasticsearch document counts and mappings are the state at the moment of the query (observed 2026-11-23T17:13Z), so they cannot prove the index contents during an earlier incident window.

The service label values here (payment-api, order-service, inventory-api) are Elasticsearch document fields, not the Jaeger/Prometheus service_name values used elsewhere; no cross-mapping to those telemetry identities was established.
next_steps: If a per-window breakdown is needed, repeat the terms aggregation with explicit start_time/end_time ranges, since the tool always applies its time filter on the 'timestamp' field and otherwise defaults to the last hour.
Clarify whether 'service' counts should be reported for the full authorized window or for a specific incident interval; the two differ (10 documents vs 2 documents in the last hour).
